about: CHAIN lost_brother (Design/content/chains/lost_brother.md): a kinsman taken in a raid and sold, followed port by port. Fourteen cards. In the summer of 810 King Godfred's two hundred ships fall on the Frisian islands (Annales regni Francorum 810). The merchant's brother Liafbern, who farms their mother's kin's mound by Doccinga, is rowed off with his son Wibern, a boy of ten. At Sliesthorp the dealer remembers the lot and how it was split: the grown men south with a Saxon drover, down the Hellweg to the Rhine and Mainz, where the Verdun men buy for Spain; the young east with a Svea to Birka, and from there to Aldeigja when the ships go. The southern road is far and its time is short (200 days); the eastern is near and its time is long (420 days): the house can reach one surely, both only by haste, and in the spring of 811 it can stand on the Eider where twelve Franks and twelve Danes swear peace and ask for something no annal records. Five endings: both home (end_both, the hard road); the brother home and the boy a Svea's boy on the east road (end_brother); the boy home and his father gone to Spain (end_boy); nobody home and a share of a mound (end_empty_bench, as it really went for the islands); and the peace sworn with the islands' people in it (end_peace, history changed: changed_eider_peace_captives). Progress is flags ch_lost_brother_1 to _9; the named flags, the timers, the endings and the grand rewards are listed in the chain page. A road that is never sailed closes by itself when ch_lost_brother_search runs out (1,300 days from the first card), so the chain always ends. The words are in Data/writing/chain_lost_brother.json; each option's note names the writing key of its outcome text (the engine shows the effects' own facts; the outcome keys are for the integrator). Nobody in the speech says 'slave trade' or 'Viking': they are the taken, a lot, a head, the heathen men, the Danes. Liafbern, Wibern, Frethburg, Ingimar and Gundbert are invented; cast.asulf, cast.dragomir, cast.holmfast are the spine's invented cast; cast.landric and Archbishop Riculf are real. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at any of six Frisian landings from midsummer 810 to the end of 812). A man off the islands brings word: the mound burned, the brother and his boy rowed off alive. Sources: Annales regni Francorum 810 (a fleet of two hundred ships from the Northmen's land; all the islands off the Frisian shore wasted; three battles; a hundred pounds of silver already paid as tribute; the king marches to the Aller and Weser; Godfred killed by one of his own following; the elephant Abul Abbas dies at Lippeham the same summer). Chronicle entries: chronicle_793.json 810-summer-frisia-raid-810, 810-summer-godfred-murdered, 810-summer-elephant-dies. That people were carried off in 810 is not in the annal (?); it is said outright of the next raid on Frisia, in 813, when the Northmen carried off men, women and much booty (Chronicle of Moissac 813; chronicle_793.json 813-frisia-raid-813). Liafbern and Wibern are invented. Sets ch_lost_brother_1 and the long timer ch_lost_brother_search (1,300 days).

cards.intention: A man with a burned hand is asking along the landing for your house by name. He is off the islands. He was your brother's neighbour, and he has been walking for nine days.

cards.note: Step 2 (drawn at Doccinga after step 1). The mound by the creek: the byre burned, the looms standing, the brother's wife Frethburg (invented) and the priest. She tells the marks to know them by. The priest tells the story of Imma. Sources: Bede, Historia ecclesiastica IV.22 (Imma, a thegn taken after the battle on the Trent in 679, whose bonds fell off whenever his brother the priest said Mass for him, and who was sold in London to a Frisian; retold in our own words, nothing quoted); the wooden church of St Paul and St Boniface on its mound at Doccinga (dossiers/doccinga.md); Frisian cloth woven on the mounds (goods_793.json frisian_cloth). The priest is cast.landric (real: Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.22; all he says is ours). Sets ch_lost_brother_2 and one of ch_lost_brother_names, ch_lost_brother_vow, ch_lost_brother_band.

options.label: Take the silver the mound has dug up for the buying back, and give your word on it
options.note: outcome: chain_lost_brother.s02.out_silver (ninety pennies in cut silver and old coin, and a word given before neighbours)

options.note: outcome: chain_lost_brother.s02.out_band (the boy will know the pattern; it can go east without you, step 9)

cards.note: Step 3 (drawn at Sliesthorp in the sailing months, after step 1). The dealer's pen behind the booths. He remembers every lot and has no reason to lie: the island lot was split. Sources: Godfred carried the merchants of Reric to Sliesthorp in 808 (Annales regni Francorum 808; spine thread godfreds_market); captives sold at Sliaswich (Vita Rimberti c. 18, of the 870s: later, used for the place only); iron shackles from Hedeby's harbour (economy/furs_amber_ivory_slaves.md 5.10); lots sold from Lammas to Martinmas (the same file, 5.4). The southern road, by the Hellweg to the Rhine and to Verdun, is attested for the tenth century (Liudprand, Antapodosis VI.6, of about 949) and read back to 810 (?). Cast: cast.asulf, cast.dragomir. A blade given here breaks the king's law (Thionville 805 c. 7); the toll man's own card is the danger, not this one. Sets ch_lost_brother_3 and the two timers: ch_lost_brother_south_open (200 days) and ch_lost_brother_east_open (420 days; 540 with the blade, because he sends word east).

cards.note: Step 4, the turn that can change history (drawn at Sliesthorp from March to June 811 only, after step 1; it does not need step 3, and the chain never waits for it). The peace of the Eider. Sources: Annales regni Francorum 811: the peace between the emperor and Hemming, sworn on weapons over the hard winter, is confirmed when the roads open by twelve great men of each people meeting on the river Eider; the Frankish twelve are led by Count Wala, son of Bernhard, the Danes by Hemming's brothers Hankwin and Angandeo (chronicle_793.json 811-spring-eider-peace). The annal gives no terms beyond the peace itself. A clause for the return of the taken is our invention and is the change: changed_eider_peace_captives. The clerk and the king's man are invented; Wala and Hemming are real and are spoken of, not met. On 'list' (needs the priest's list from step 2) the clause is likely sworn; failing, the king's man gives his token for the dealer. On 'speak' (needs half the Northmen's tongue and a name known here) it is sworn. Sets ch_lost_brother_4.

cards.title: Twelve and twelve
cards.intention: The town is full of horses. A day's ride west, on the Eider, twelve great men of the Franks and twelve of the Danes are to swear the peace the kings made over the winter. A Frankish clerk is buying fish and writing down what it cost. One of King Hemming's men is watching him write.

cards.note: Step 5, a side step on the southern road (drawn at Diusburg after step 3, while the brother's road is open). The ferry at the Ruhr's mouth, where the Hellweg from Saxony comes down to the Rhine. The ferryman counted the drover's lot across and saw one of the 'Wends' cross himself. Sources: Diusburg at the west end of the Hellweg (dossiers/diusburg.md); Herstal 779 c. 19: a sale of people is made before the bishop or the count, the archdeacon, the hundred-man or the count's judge, or before well-known witnesses, and nobody sells one beyond the march (MGH Capit. I no. 20). That a lot from Sliesthorp walked this road in 810 is our invention (?). Sets ch_lost_brother_5; 'witness' sets ch_lost_brother_witness, which makes the oath at Mainz sure.

ferryman.note: the ferryman at the Ruhr's mouth (invented)

cards.title: One who crossed himself
cards.intention: The road from Saxony comes down to the water here, and whatever walks it crosses in this man's boat. He counts everything he carries, because he is paid by the head, for oxen and for people alike.

options.label: Pay him thirty pennies to come up the river and say it under oath
options.note: outcome: chain_lost_brother.s05.out_witness (a well-known witness, as the law of Herstal asks)

options.label: Ask him what else the road has brought down, and go on
options.note: outcome: chain_lost_brother.s05.out_ask (a true price word: the cloth boats are late and Mainz is paying over)

memory.witness: hired him as a witness for Mainz
memory.ask: asked after a lot of Wends

cards.note: Step 6, the southern road in time (drawn at Mogontia within 200 days of step 3). The lot stands in a Verdun merchant's yard by the Frisians' quarter, to be sold on before the archbishop's steward as the law asks. The brother is in it, sworn a heathen Wend by the drover. Sources: Herstal 779 c. 19 (as step 5); Lex Frisionum XXI, on man-stealing: who sells a free man out of the country pays for him as if he had killed him, or brings him back (the law was set down about 802; the wording is from memory (?)); the test of a Christian by what he can say (the nun who sang psalms at Sliaswich, Vita Rimberti c. 18: later, the idea only); Archbishop Riculf of Mainz, 787 to 9 August 813, then Haistulf (dossiers/mogontia.md); the Frisian quarter at Mainz (ports_793.json; Annales Fuldenses 886 for its burning: later). Verdun's merchants and the road to Spain: Liudprand, Antapodosis VI.6 (about 949), read back (?). Gundbert and the steward are invented. A man's price of 300 d is the top of the evidence (120 to 240 d) and a Verdun price. The share of 160 d paid to the kinsman who proves the wrong is ours (?). Sets ch_lost_brother_6, ch_lost_brother_brother_free and the wait ch_lost_brother_wait_home (40 days); 'witness' and a won 'oath' set the lasting cost ch_lost_brother_verdun_grudge; 'alms' and a lost 'oath' set ch_lost_brother_church_debt.

cards.note: Step 7, the southern road too late (drawn at Mogontia once the 200 days have run). The yard is empty: the lot went up the Mosel road to Verdun, and from Verdun such lots go down the Saone and Rhone to Spain. Sources: Liudprand, Antapodosis VI.6 (about 949: Verdun's merchants and Spain; read back (?)); Agobard of Lyon's letters of about 826 tell of a man who came back from Cordoba twenty-four years after he was stolen and sold as a boy (from memory (?); later; the idea only). What becomes of the letter or the writ is not told here: the house learns it at its own door (steps 10 to 14). Sets ch_lost_brother_7 and either ch_lost_brother_brother_free or ch_lost_brother_brother_lost, with a long wait.

cards.note: Step 8, the eastern road in time (drawn at Birka in the open months, within 420 days of step 3, or 540 with the dealer's word). The boy herds a Svea shipman's sheep on the island and bails his boat. Sources: Birka a market for people as for furs, and Christian captives there glad of a priest in 829 (Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 11); a bondwoman at one mark of silver (Laxdaela saga c. 12: thirteenth century, of about 950; the only northern price), so about 125 d; wine dear at Birka (goods_793.json rhenish_wine wanted svealand 3). Cast: cast.holmfast, who points the way and vouches for a stick. Ingimar is invented (Ingi- and -mar, both on the rune stones of Uppland). Sets ch_lost_brother_8, ch_lost_brother_boy_free and the wait ch_lost_brother_wait_home (40 days); a paid option brings the turn's reward, an order for cloth at a premium.

cards.note: Step 9, the eastern road too late (drawn at Birka once the days have run). The shipman took the boy east as his ship's boy after midsummer; he winters at Aldeigja. Sources: the east road from Birka to Aldeigjuborg and the dirhams from about 800 (spine thread silver_road; realms/rus.json); Findan of Leinster, taken about 845 and passed from ship to ship (his Life: later; the idea that a taken boy becomes a ship's boy). Cast: cast.holmfast, who will carry silver or a token and take a fee. What the boy answers is not told here: the house learns it at its own door. Sets ch_lost_brother_9 and either ch_lost_brother_boy_free or ch_lost_brother_boy_lost with ch_lost_brother_boy_east, and a long wait.

cards.note: FINALE, ending end_both: the hard road (drawn at Doccinga when both are free and the wait has run, if the peace clause was not sworn; with the clause the finale is step 14). Brother and boy at the mound. What a Frisian of 810 could really win: a brother as a sworn partner in a second boat (kin partnerships are the ordinary Frisian house); a brother's son fostered into the boat; a store on the mound and its weaving. Sources: Frisian cloth (goods_793.json); the kin's duty to ransom and the kin's share (Lex Frisionum, in general (?)). Sets ch_lost_brother_end_both and ch_lost_brother_done; grand rewards: unlock_partner_liafbern and unlock_kin_wibern on 'partner' and 'nothing' (two, the hard road), 'nothing' adds unlock_plot_doccinga; 'weave' gives unlock_factor_doccinga and unlock_kin_wibern.

cards.note: FINALE, ending end_empty_bench: as it really went (drawn at Doccinga when neither is free and both roads are closed, by choice or by time, if the peace clause was not sworn). No annal says that anyone taken from the islands in 810 came home. The lost man's share of the mound falls to his kin. Sources: Annales regni Francorum 810 and 811 (no return of anyone is recorded); the church of St Paul and St Boniface at Doccinga (dossiers/doccinga.md); Masses for the absent as in Bede IV.22. That a brother inherits before a wife is our reading of Frisian custom (?). Sets ch_lost_brother_end_empty_bench and ch_lost_brother_done; grand reward unlock_plot_doccinga ('share'), unlock_factor_doccinga ('widow') or unlock_title_st_bonifaces_man ('masses').

cards.note: FINALE, ending end_peace: history changed (drawn at Doccinga after the clause was sworn on the Eider, once both roads of the house's own kin are closed one way or the other). What is real: the peace of 811 has no known terms, Hemming died in 812, and nobody taken in 810 is known to have come home. What is changed (changed_eider_peace_captives): the peace binds the Danish king to give back the islands' people still in his kingdom and to make good the price of those sold out of it; boats come from the Eider at Lammas; the mounds are peopled again. The house's own two were sold beyond the Danes before the oath, so the clause brings silver for them and not the people: who is at the table depends on steps 6 to 9. The Danish king's peace for one Frisian boat at Sliesthorp is modelled on the later talks of 873, when the Danes asked that merchants might cross the march in peace (Annales Fuldenses 873). Sets ch_lost_brother_end_peace and ch_lost_brother_done; grand reward unlock_title_islands_spokesman on every option; 'charter' adds unlock_charter_sliesthorp, 'partner' adds unlock_partner_liafbern.

cards.title: The boats from the Eider
cards.intention: There is smoke from every mound along the creek. The boats came at Lammas: thirty-one people of the forty-three on the priest's tablet, thin, and counted off the gunwale by a Dane with a tally stick. He is still here. He has a bag of weighed silver for the names that could not be found, and two of those names are yours.
